title: Operational Reliability Hypothesis Lab - cross-team experiments
content:
Context:
This doc captures the hypothesis-driven experiments we want to run across platform, serving-runtime, and observability teams to validate operational levers for improving SLO attainment without doubling costs. Treat as a lightweight lab plan + running notes.

Executive summary:
- Problem: Several customer-facing model endpoints have intermittent latency spikes during tail-query patterns and correlated availability blips when autoscaler churns. We need pragmatic mitigations that preserve cost targets.
- Goal: Run 4 focused experiments over 8 weeks to measure the impact of: (1) conservative autoscaler hysteresis, (2) adaptive KV-cache warming, (3) prefix-based routing to warm shards, (4) emergency soft-fallback model variant routing.
- Success criteria: 20% reduction in 95th percentile latency for target endpoints and <5% increment in monthly GPU-hour bill for the pilot workspace.

Scope and constraints:
- Pilot services: hosted-api/model-serving tier (routes: chat-stream-v2, gen-short). Exclude internal infra-only endpoints.
- Stakeholders: SRE (lead), serving-runtime (implementation), observability (telemetry), product-hosted-api (product owner), platform-engineering (autoscaler changes).
- Safety constraints: No permanent removal of autoscaling safeguards; all changes behind feature flags; rollback playbook required.

Hypotheses (priority order):
1) Autoscaler hysteresis reduces scale flapping and downstream tail latency. Measure: number of scale-up/scale-down events per hour; 95p latency.
2) Adaptive KV-cache warming for bursty prefixes reduces cold-KV latency. Measure: cache hit ratio for prefix and tail-latency.
3) Prefix-aware routing (sticky routing for frequent prefixes) reduces cold-starts with modest eviction impact. Measure: collision rate and latency delta.
4) Soft-fallback to quantized model variant during resource pressure reduces error budget burn without severe quality regressions. Measure: fallback rate, quality metric on eval set, cost delta.

Experiment matrix (week-by-week):
- Week 1 (setup): feature-flag scaffolding, telemetry dashboards (obs team), canary route selection. Create baseline capture (2 weeks of med/95/99 latencies, scale events).
- Week 2-3 (autoscaler hysteresis A/B): implement conservative cooldown in a fraction of pods (canary slice 5%). Rollout 2-week A/B, collect scale event counts, latencies, costs.
- Week 4 (KV-cache pilot): server-side adaptive prefetch for top-50 prefixes for selected routes. Test in canary for 1 week, then broaden.
- Week 5-6 (prefix-aware routing): implement sticky routing policy for top-10 prefixes, monitor shard hotness.
- Week 7 (soft-fallback): implement routing to quantized variant under CPU/GPU pressure triggers. Run controlled experiments against synthetic load and small percentage of production traffic.
- Week 8 (analysis + retro): consolidate metrics, risk review, decide next steps.

Telemetry and success metrics (owner in parens):
- Latency P95 and P99 per-route (observability)
- Scale events per 1k requests (platform-engineering)
- GPU-hour delta for pilot (finance+platform)
- Cache hit rate and KV latency (serving-runtime)
- QoR on eval prompts for fallback variant (applied-ml/product)
- Alert churn (SRE)

Instrumentation checklist before each experiment:
- Tag requests with experiment-id header
- Add tracers for cache-warm / fallback decisions
- Export scale events to metrics pipeline with labels (route, zone, experiment)
- Synthetic test harness to replay representative prefixes (dev infra)

Rollout policy and safety (must-haves):
- All changes behind flags with automatic kill-switch (feature flag + monitoring alerts).
- Immediate rollback criteria: 50% rise in error-rate or >20% increase in 95p latency sustained for 10 minutes.
- Escalation path documented: SRE pager -> platform oncall -> serving-runtime oncall.

Open risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Sticky routing increases shard imbalance -> mitigation: shard-eviction policy, cap sticky sessions to top-k prefixes.
- Risk: Fallback model causes degraded generation -> mitigation: A/B test with labelled evaluation + user-facing QA; circuit-breaker to disable if quality delta > threshold.
- Risk: Telemetry gap -> mitigation: obs team to block experiment start until required spans/metrics exist.

Decision log (running):
- 2026-12-05: Kickoff, hypotheses prioritized.
- 2026-12-06: Obs agreed to add experiment labels to trace payloads (Miguel).
- 2026-12-08: Platform agreed to build canary slice mechanism for autoscaler tests (Priya).

Next steps (owners):
- SRE (Aisha): finalize rollback playbook and runbook snippets, draft oncall scripts.
- Observability (Miguel): create dashboard template + alerts, ensure metric cardinality controls.
- Serving-runtime (Tomoko): prototype KV prefetch for prefix set, instrument code paths.
- Platform (Priya): implement canary autoscaler cooldown and traffic-split mechanics.
- Applied ML (Ethan): prepare eval set and quality gating for fallback variant.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider integrating a short-lived traffic shadowing experiment to validate fallback quality without user impact.
- If prefix distribution is very skewed, explore multi-tenant shard allocation vs. prefix affinity.
